subject: TimeBridge: coordinating global hands-on POC + load test windows
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Aligning hands-on POC windows across US/EU/APAC

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Acme is excited to get the POC kicked off. We'd like to book a set of hands-on working sessions (prompt review, routing config, and a short load test) that work across our teams in SF, London, and Singapore. Our priorities are:

- Prompt walkthrough and example prompt set validation (60m)
- Routing/topology and model variant review (45m)
- Load test rehearsal (75m, with a ten-minute scaling/ramp)

To avoid burning too many cycles across timezones we were hoping Redwood could propose a rotating schedule that gives each region at least one hands-on overlap window with your engineers. We sketched three candidate windows that would work for our cross-functional attendees — attached is a rough agenda (POC-agenda-v1.pdf).

Candidate windows (local offsets):
1) Early APAC / Late EU: 01:00–03:00 PDT (09:00–11:00 BST / 16:00–18:00 SGT)
2) US midday overlap: 11:00–14:00 PDT (19:00–22:00 BST)
3) EU morning / US late: 07:00–10:00 PDT (15:00–18:00 BST)

Can you confirm which of these you can staff? We can be flexible on order if you prefer to anchor a recurring "bridge hour" for handoffs. Also, we'd like the load test to happen in the middle day of the POC week — ideally a time when both the US and EU engineers can join for the first 30 mins of the ramp.

Attaching the agenda. We can share calendar invites once we lock times.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Applied ML, Acme AI
alice@acme.ai

Attachment: POC-agenda-v1.pdf (13KB, PDF stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 14:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Aligning hands-on POC windows across US/EU/APAC

Hi Alice — great to hear and thanks for the clear priorities. Dylan and Jonas looped in since they'll lead the hands-on sessions.

We propose a TimeBridge schedule pattern that reduces context switching for our engineers while giving each region a useful overlap hour. High level:

- Day 1: Prompt review anchored to EU morning / US late (we do the walkthrough and collect prompt set feedback)
- Day 2: Routing & model variant review anchored to US midday overlap (config deep-dive + quick fallback tests)
- Day 3: Load test rehearsal in a rolling window that starts in US midday and hands off to EU (we'll do the 75m ramp, with first 30m monitored synchronously by US+EU)

Concrete staffing:
- We can staff Jonas for the prompt session (EU-friendly), Dylan for routing + load orchestration (US midday).
- Suggested concrete times (PDT):
  * Prompt review: Day 1 07:00–08:15 PDT (15:00–16:15 BST / 23:00–00:15 SGT) — shorter prompt slot to focus on examples.
  * Routing review: Day 2 11:00–12:00 PDT (19:00–20:00 BST) — config, routing rules, failover plan.
  * Load test rehearsal: Day 3 11:30–13:15 PDT (19:30–21:15 BST) — 10m ramp, 65m steady-state. We will open a 30m overlap buffer at the start for the US/EU engineers.

I attached a compact availability grid showing who can cover which slots this week (availability-grid.csv). If any of the proposed PDT times are hard for Acme, tell us which region/time you prefer to anchor and we can flip the order.

Next steps:
- Can Acme confirm preferred order and which specific attendees will join each session?
- We'll create timeboxed calendar invites for the three sessions and a shared doc for prompts + routing snippets.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: availability-grid.csv (2KB, CSV stub)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning hands-on POC windows across US/EU/APAC

Marissa — all sounds good. A couple quick operational notes for the load test slot so Acme has expectations:

- For a realistic rehearsal we'll run a burst that simulates your anticipated concurrency and then hold a steady qps for ~60m. Please list peak concurrent sessions in the shared doc; that determines whether we route through Dedicated pools or our shared hosted fleet.
- We'll include a 15m post-test sync to review logs and any reroute events.
- Suggest we make the first 30m of the prompt session explicitly "pair-programming" style: Jonas + Acme prompt authors to iterate live examples. That helps us capture exact prefix/KV caching behavior.

If Acme can share an example prompt set ahead of Day 1 (even 10–15 prompts), Jonas and I can pre-run them with two model variants so we have concrete comparison notes in the session.

I'll stand up the load harness and a short checklist for the test run.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai

From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Bob Lee <bob@acme.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 09:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Aligning hands-on POC windows across US/EU/APAC

Marissa / Dylan / Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear plan. Bob and I reviewed the concrete times and the order you suggested works for us. A few quick confirmations: 

- We'll provide a 12–15 prompt seed set by EOD Monday (links in the shared doc).
- Peak concurrent sessions for the load test: target 150 concurrent sessions, with a 5x burst expected during the first 10m.
- Attendees: Alice Nguyen (lead ML), Bob Lee (infra lead), Priya Shah (SRE, joining the load test), and two product owners who will sit in the prompt review.

Please send calendar invites for the three sessions and include the shared doc + the HubSpot deal link in the invite. We also need a short pre-POC checklist (we prefer a 1‑pager) that covers access, keys, and data handling specifics.

If you want a quick pre-POC sync with our infra folks, Bob is available Tue afternoon BST.

I'll mark this confirmed on our side. Looking forward to getting hands-on.

Best,
Alice
Head of Applied ML, Acme AI
alice@acme.ai
